general_information.Description: This course equips students with knowledge of the C++ programming language from basic to advanced, *) Basics - C++ Keywords, C++ Variable Types, Lvalues and Rvalues, Operators in C++, Strings, Arrrays, Pointerts, C++ References, C++ Basic Input/Output ... - OOP *) Advance: C/C++ Standard Template Libaries, Files/streaming ,Exception, template, multithread, smartpointer, etc.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all assigned exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose. - Promptly access to the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand and apply fundamental concepts of C++ programming to develop basic computational solutions
Effectively manage memory and organize data using advanced C++ programming techniques
Write modular, reusable, and efficient C++ programs using advanced programming techniques and standard libraries.
Apply object-oriented programming principles and techniques in C++ to design robust, modular, and maintainable software solutions.
Apply advanced C++ programming features and file handling techniques to develop flexible and efficient software solutions.

schedule.Topic: Introduction to C++ and Development Environment
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 1 - Introduction to C++ and Basic Syntax
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Write a “Hello, World!” program. - Modify the program to print user-inputted text.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 1 - Introduction to C++ and Basic Syntax
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Debug and fix syntax errors in a provided C++ program. - Use cout and cin for basic input/output operations.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 1 - Introduction to C++ and Basic Syntax
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Declare variables and perform basic arithmetic operations. - Use constants to store fixed values.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 2 - Operators, Expressions, and Basic I/O
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Write a program to calculate the area of a rectangle. - Implement logical expressions for simple decision-making.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 2 - Operators, Expressions, and Basic I/O
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Predict and fix unexpected results due to operator precedence. - Implement explicit type conversion using static_cast<>.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 2 - Operators, Expressions, and Basic I/O
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Create a basic calculator using arithmetic operators. - Read and print user information (name, age, and city).

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 3 - Control Structures - Decision Making and Loops
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Write a program to check if a number is even or odd. - Implement a grading system using switch-case.

schedule.Topic: Looping Constructs & Nested Loops and Logical Flow
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 3 - Control Structures – Decision Making and Loops
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Write a program to print the first N Fibonacci numbers. - Implement a countdown timer using loops. - Implement a simple multiplication table generator. - Write a program to print a pyramid pattern using *.

schedule.Student Materials: Lab's questions
Slides - Slot 4 - Arrays and Pointer Fundamentals
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Find the maximum and minimum values in an array. - Reverse an array.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 4 - Arrays and Pointer Fundamentals
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Swap two numbers using pointers. - Implement a function to reverse an array using pointers.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 4 - Arrays and Pointer Fundamentals
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a function that returns a pointer to the largest element in an array. - Demonstrate pointer-based iteration through a two-dimensional array.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 5 - Dynamic Memory Allocation & Advanced Pointer Usage
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Create a dynamic array and fill it with user input. - Implement a simple dynamic list with manual memory allocation.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 5 - Dynamic Memory Allocation & Advanced Pointer Usage
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Demonstrate a scenario where a memory leak occurs, then fix it. - Implement a function that safely reallocates an array.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 5 - Dynamic Memory Allocation & Advanced Pointer Usage
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a dynamically allocated matrix and perform basic operations. - Develop a simple memory-efficient data storage system.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 6 - Structs, Unions, and Complex Data Organization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Define a Student struct and store multiple students' information. - Sort an array of structs based on GPA.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 6 - Structs, Unions, and Complex Data Organization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a union to store either an integer or a float in minimal memory.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 6 - Structs, Unions, and Complex Data Organization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Define a Library struct where each book has multiple authors. - Write and read struct data from a file.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 7 - Memory Management and Performance Optimization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a program that dynamically allocates and deallocates memory efficiently.

schedule.Topic: Smart Pointers and RAII Performance Optimization and Best Practices
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 7 - Memory Management and Performance Optimization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Convert a raw pointer-based program to use smart pointers. - Analyze and optimize a sample C++ program for better memory efficiency.

schedule.Student Materials: Lab's questions
Slides - Slot 8 - Functions, Overloading, and Template Programming
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a function to calculate the factorial of a number. - Create a function to find the greatest common divisor (GCD) using recursion.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 8 - Functions, Overloading, and Template Programming
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement an overloaded function for calculating areas of different shapes. - Use default parameters for flexible function behavior.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 8 - Functions, Overloading, and Template Programming
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a function template for finding the maximum of two values. - Create a simple class template for handling an array of any data type.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 9 - Scope, Namespaces, and Visibility Rules
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Demonstrate variable scope using static and global variables. - Implement a program that manages variables across multiple files.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 9 - Scope, Namespaces, and Visibility Rules
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a program using multiple namespaces for different modules. - Use namespace to organize a library system.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 9 - Scope, Namespaces, and Visibility Rules
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement encapsulation in a C++ class with getter/setter functions. - Control access to class members in a real-world scenario.

schedule.Topic: Overview of Standard Library (STL) & Common Containers
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 10 - Introduction to STL Containers & Algorithms
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a dynamic list using std::vector. - Store and retrieve key-value pairs using std::map.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 10 - Introduction to STL Containers & Algorithms
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Sort and search elements in a std::vector. - Implement a simple contact management system using std::map.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 10 - Introduction to STL Containers & Algorithms
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a task manager using std::queue. - Demonstrate stack-based undo functionality.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 11 - Introduction to STL Features & Optimization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Use lambda functions to apply transformations on a std::vector. - Implement custom sorting criteria using lambdas.

schedule.Topic: STL Performance Considerations & Optimization. Real-World STL Applications.
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 11 - Introduction to STL Features & Optimization
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Optimize an existing program by choosing the right STL container. - Implement a high-performance data processing application using STL. - Develop a student record system using map, vector, and STL algorithms. - Implement a real-time event processing system using queue and priority_queue.

schedule.Student Materials: Lab's questions
Slides - Slot 12 - Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Encapsulation
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Define a Car class with attributes (brand, model, year). - Create and manipulate objects from the class.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 12 - Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Encapsulation
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement encapsulation in a BankAccount class with private balance. - Use constructors to initialize object values.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 12 - Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) & Encapsulation
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Create a Student class with static member to count students. - Implement a method to update object attributes dynamically.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 13 - Inheritance - Code Reusability & Hierarchical Design
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Create a Person class and inherit Student and Teacher from it. - Demonstrate different access levels in inheritance.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 13 - Inheritance - Code Reusability & Hierarchical Design
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement multi-level inheritance (Animal → Mammal → Dog). - Use constructor chaining to initialize derived class attributes.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 13 - Inheritance - Code Reusability & Hierarchical Design
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Create a Shape class with draw() method and override it in Circle and Rectangle. - Implement runtime polymorphism using pointers to base class.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 14 - Polymorphism & Special Member Functions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Overload + operator to add two Complex numbers. - Implement << and >> operators for easy input/output.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 14 - Polymorphism & Special Member Functions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Demonstrate object copying with copy constructor. - Optimize memory using move constructor.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 14 - Polymorphism & Special Member Functions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Demonstrate object destruction in polymorphic class hierarchy. - Convert raw pointer-based code to use unique_ptr.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 15 - Exception Handling & Robust Application Design
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement division by zero exception handling. - Handle invalid user input in a number conversion program.

schedule.Topic: Handling Multiple Exceptions & Custom Exceptions, Exception Safety
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 15 - Exception Handling & Robust Application Design
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement exception handling for array index out of bounds. - Create a BankTransaction class with a custom exception for insufficient balance. - Use RAII for managing dynamic memory safely.

schedule.Student Materials: Lab's questions

schedule.Topic: Introduction to File I/O & Text File Handling
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 16 - Text File Handling & Basic File Operations
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Write a program to store and retrieve student records from a text file. - Implement a simple logging system that appends messages to a file.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 16 - Text File Handling & Basic File Operations
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Develop a contact book where users can add and search contacts. - Implement a CSV parser to read structured text data.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 16 - Text File Handling & Basic File Operations
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Optimize file reading operations for better efficiency. - Identify and fix common file handling errors in sample code.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 17 - Binary File Handling & File Processing
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a program to store and retrieve employee records in binary format. - Demonstrate random access file operations (seekg, seekp, tellg, tellp).

schedule.Topic: File Processing – Searching, Updating, and Deleting
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 17 - Binary File Handling & File Processing
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a basic student management system that allows adding, updating, and deleting records. - Create a binary-based inventory system that maintains product details.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 17 - Binary File Handling & File Processing
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement a file-based caching system to reduce read/write overhead. - Optimize an existing file handling program for better performance.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 18 - Preprocessor Directives & Type Conversions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement header guards to prevent multiple inclusions. - Use #define macros for constant expressions and debugging.

schedule.Topic: Type Casting and Type Conversion Operators
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 18 - Preprocessor Directives & Type Conversions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement custom type conversion for a Temperature class (Celsius ↔ Fahrenheit). - Use dynamic_cast for safe downcasting in an OOP hierarchy.

schedule.Topic: Best Practices for Type Safety & Optimization
schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 18 - Preprocessor Directives & Type Conversions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Optimize memory usage by choosing appropriate data types for calculations. - Debug a program with incorrect type conversions and apply correct casting.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 19 - Smart Pointers, Multithreading, and Lambda Expressions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Convert raw pointer-based memory management to smart pointers. - Demonstrate circular reference issues and solve them using weak_ptr.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 19 - Smart Pointers, Multithreading, and Lambda Expressions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Implement multithreading to execute multiple tasks in parallel. - Use mutex to prevent race conditions in shared data.

schedule.Student Materials: Slides - Slot 19 - Smart Pointers, Multithreading, and Lambda Expressions
schedule.Student's Tasks: Hands-on exercises: - Use lambda functions for dynamic sorting and filtering. - Implement a callback mechanism using function pointers and lambdas.
